newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up amid lists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end up amid lists.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices ended 1/4 to 3/8 of a point higher as bid lists--totaling $500 million by one estimate--drew aggressive bids, traders said.
"There were a lot of lists but all the lists got very good numbers, strong numbers," one trader said.

"I would say the majority of the customer bid wanteds were traded, and there was also a decent amount of Street bid wanted," the trader said, adding that he did not stop to tally them. "I got sick of bidding it actually."

Municipals were "following the government market to be honest with you," the trader said. "I mean I don't think there is any underlying great big demand in our market, but there is some demand," he said.
Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which yielded no change in interest rates, kept participants on hold, but now they are back in, the trader said.
Another trader felt the Fed should have tightened rates.

"I actually thought it was kind of a bearish development over the long haul, but it looks like the market, in the short-term anyway, thinks it's a good thing," he said. "I would liked to have seen them get it out of the way, whether it was 25 (basis points), or whether it was 50."
In debt futures, the December municipal contract ended up 10/32 at 113-30/32. The December T-bond contract ended up 19/32 at 109-7/32. The MOB spread was 151 ticks.

Wednesday's negotiated action saw Goldman Sachs & Co reprice $142.3 million Port of Portland, Ore., airport bonds, cutting yields in several maturities and lowering the top yield in 2026 to 5.93 percent from 5.97 percent.
Bear Stearns & Co said it repriced $79.4 million Battery Park City Authority, N.Y., junior revenue bonds, cutting the top yield in 2029 to 5.83 percent from 5.875 percent.
Looking ahead, the New York State Urban Development Corp plans to sell about $600 million of refunding bonds around the week of Oct. 7. PaineWebber Inc will handle the sale.
In addition, Harris County, Texas, Commissioners Court on Tuesday approved plans to sell roughly $250 million bonds in late October, a county official said.

The negotiated offering is expected to consist of about $80 million of refunding bonds and about $165 million of new money, she said. Goldman Sachs & Co. will serve as bookrunning senior manager, with Smith Barney Inc as co-senior manager, the official said.
On the competitive side, the District of Columbia said it has postponed a $168.87 million general obligation bond sale till roughly October 3. The deal had been scheduled for Thursday.

The city will announce the exact issue date via news wire services at least 24 hours before the sale. The District postponed the sale to give Congress more time to enact a bill that would waive a current 30-day congressional review requirement for pending D.C. bond sales.
